text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
- Three intelligence officers have been charged with violating state secrets while handling the Birch Tree case.
- Beefed up police presence on the streets of Budapest hjas resulted in a drop of the number of crimes.
- A member of the board of radio trustees has resigned on Monday saying that the state radio's news coverage is narrow, biased and intolerant.
Slovakia sent a proposal to Hungary on a joint minority committe ahead of the two prime ministers' meetig on August 15.
- Agriculture Minister Frigyes Nagy said Hungary's wheat crop will be about five million tonnes this year but of lower quality than usual.
- Industrial production rose 15.1 percent yera-on-year in June and was up 3.8 percent month-on-month.
A drop in the purchasing manager index (PMI) showed a slowdown in economic growth.
- Steel mill Dunaferr has signed a three billion forints loan agreement.
- National electricity company MVM Rt is expected to sign a contract to buy electricity from Matrai power station.
- Hungary has the most developed real estate market in central and eastern Europe.
- The losing bidder for TV concessions, CME, said it is looking qat alternative ways to get into commercial broadcasting.
